theFix.sourceStringIntroduced: STAMP_SOURCE = "legacy-design-tools:txgio_parcel.zoning_district" (src/jobs/parcel-r5-zoning.mjs). Names what it names because that is literally where the value comes from: legacy-design-tools' stampCountyZoning() (lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-stamp-db.ts) UPDATEs txgio_parcel.zoning_district from an in-memory index built from LDT's OWN zoning-layers.ts registry -- confirmed by direct read of that file's UPDATE statement, never by inference. Deliberately not ZONING_SOURCE (tx_zoning_district_staging): that table is populated only by hauska-engine's stage-tx-zoning-district.mjs from hauska-engine's OWN, separate zoning-staging registry (CTX-STAMP's finding), and this value never passed through it. Using ZONING_SOURCE would have been the exact false-provenance claim this program's whole gate structure exists to prevent.
theFix.howBuilt: RESIDUE_HAS_REAL_ZONING_SQL (CTX-PARCELGATE's own eligibility query) reused unmodified as the sole eligibility decision -- its EXISTS gate is byte-for-byte identical to before, still enforced by the pre-existing pinned SQL-shape test. Widened (not duplicated) with three correlated scalar subqueries, same predicate, LIMIT 1 ordered by feature_index, to also return zoning_district/zoning_jurisdiction/ingested_at in the SAME round trip -- 'one definition, two consumers' per the dispatch, rather than a second, independently-derived query that could drift from it. loadResidueWithRealZoning's return type widened from Set<string> to Map<string,{districtCode,jurisdiction,ingestedAt}>; every existing call site's membership check (.has) still works identically. buildStampSourcedCells writes all three zoning-group rails (zoningDistrict/zoningJurisdictionKey/zoningProvenance) as {kind:'value'}, matching buildZoningCells' own three-rail grouping for a real match. zoningProvenance's value is a plain descriptive string (STAMP_PROVENANCE_TEXT), never a fabricated URL -- txgio_parcel captures no per-parcel source URL for the LDT stamp, and inventing one would be exactly the false-provenance risk STAMP_SOURCE exists to avoid.

stampCurrency.whatWasEstablished: A real, live-confirmed LOWER BOUND on the stamp's age, never an exact stamp date. No stronger claim is made anywhere in the shipped code or this close.
stampCurrency.how: Checked the schema (lib/db/src/schema/txgioParcel.ts) and every write path (zoning-stamp-db.ts's UPDATE, zoning-cli.ts's CLI) end to end: no column records when zoning_district was stamped, and the CLI persists no audit/run log anywhere (only console.log to whatever ran it). Found instead that legacy-design-tools' geometry-ingest CLI wholesale-replaces a county's txgio_parcel rows on every run (replaceCountyParcels: DELETE the county's rows, then a fresh batch INSERT via upsertTxgioParcels whose onConflictDoUpdate SET list excludes zoning_district and zoning_jurisdiction entirely -- confirmed by direct read of ingest.ts). Because the write path is DELETE-then-fresh-INSERT (never a plain UPSERT against a still-live row), a county-wide geometry re-ingest necessarily nulls zoning_district on every row it touches. Therefore: a row's zoning_district being non-null TODAY proves the stamp ran strictly AFTER that row's own ingested_at (the timestamp of the last full geometry replace for that county) -- a real, derivable floor, not an assumption.

stampCurrency.liveBugFoundAndFixed: The first live run against real production data (not the string-literal test fixtures) exposed that node-postgres returns a timestamptz as a JS Date object; stampCurrencyNote's original template-literal interpolation of a raw Date rendered via Date.prototype.toString() -- a locale/timezone-shifted string, not the UTC ISO instant. Fixed by normalizing ingested_at to an ISO string at loadResidueWithRealZoning's DB-read boundary (before any consumer sees it); re-ran the live probe and confirmed clean ISO strings throughout; added a regression test using a real Date instance (not a string fixture) so this exact class of bug -- correct against every hand-written fixture, wrong against real driver output -- cannot silently return.

directAnswer_bastropAndTravis.bastrop_48021: NO, not by itself -- and this is the fourth thing this close is required to surface, not a clean close. Live-measured today (method below, not by subtraction): Bastrop's RAW layer-gap residue is 26, not the 36 CTX-PARCELGATE measured earlier the same day. That drop is consistent with CTX-SP (staging Elgin's Travis-side S-P code into hauska-engine's zoning-staging registry) having landed and been re-staged since CTX-PARCELGATE's close -- 26 = 9 genuinely-uncovered + 17 staleness + 0 S-P, and CTX-PARCELGATE's own bastropCeilingPending named exactly 26 as the post-engine-fix candidate. But Bastrop's DECLARED ceiling in code is still 9 (CTX-PARCELGATE's original, correctly untouched by this card per its explicit constraint), and 26 > 9, so assertResidueWithinDeclaration still throws LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED for the combined Elgin invocation -- confirmed live, in the same run that verified this card's own fix. Nothing in Bastrop's zoningDistrict-family rails gets a real production write today because the job-level call never completes for Elgin without first re-deriving Bastrop's ceiling to >= 26, a change this card is explicitly forbidden from making (that re-derivation is CTX-PARCELGATE's own already-named, not-yet-landed follow-on). Once that ceiling IS re-derived, Bastrop's own unaccountedCount reaching zero is then a STRUCTURAL guarantee of this card's fix (every residual parcel of a declared-layer-gap city resolves to exactly one of {stamp-sourced value, refused} once the county-level guard permits the write at all) -- not a further open question.
directAnswer_bastropAndTravis.travis_48453: YES structurally, with one real caveat about how the job is invoked. Travis's ceiling is already written at 506 (CTX-PARCELGATE part 2), and this card's own fix is sufficient by itself: live-measured today, Travis's raw residue is UNCHANGED at exactly 506 (0 S-P parcels there, so CTX-SP landing had no effect on Travis, as expected), which does not exceed its ceiling. Every one of Travis's 506 residual parcels now resolves to exactly one of {stamp-sourced value (the 50 staleness parcels), refused layer-gap (the 456 genuinely-uncovered)} -- confirmed both by the per-row code path (buildStampSourcedCells and buildLayerGapCells are mutually exclusive per parcel by construction) and live, in the same real-data run. THE CAVEAT: Elgin is processed as ONE grouped city spanning both counties (CTX-ZONESCOPE's fix), not two independent per-county calls, and CITY_ALL_PARCELS_SQL orders by county_fips then prop_id, so Bastrop's parcels are chunked and processed (and, in a real --apply run, WRITTEN) before Travis's. Confirmed live: all 11 chunks covering BOTH counties (5455 in-city parcels) fully processed and their would-be writes captured BEFORE the final per-county guard loop threw on Bastrop -- the guard runs strictly after all per-chunk work, by design (the module's own existing comment: 'runs after the writes for this city, which is deliberate'). So in a real apply=true run today, Travis's real UPDATEs would land and its own rail would in fact reach unaccountedCount=0 -- but the combined Elgin job invocation would still terminate as FAILED (exit_kind:'failed', reason LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED) because Bastrop's stale ceiling throws afterward. Any system treating 'the Elgin job run succeeded' as the completion signal for Travis would be wrong until Bastrop's ceiling is also addressed, even though Travis's own data is already correct. This nuance is reported plainly because it is exactly the shape of finding this program's gate structure is built to catch, not to paper over.

scratch.text: A live run against real production data caught a bug that every hand-written string-literal test fixture missed: node-postgres returns timestamptz as a JS Date, and naively template-literal-interpolating it produces a locale/timezone-shifted Date.toString(), not an ISO instant. Normalize any DB-read timestamp to a string explicitly, at the read boundary, before it reaches any prose-generating function -- do not trust a test fixture that only ever passes a string literal to stand in for what the real driver returns.

When a dispatch says 'reuse query X, one definition two consumers,' the safest reading (least invasive to existing pinned tests, no risk of two independently-derived predicates drifting) is: keep the query's core decision predicate byte-for-byte, widen its SELECT list with correlated scalar subqueries reusing the SAME predicate text, rather than adding a second round-trip query scoped to the first's already-decided membership set. The latter looked cleaner in the abstract but would have required touching cortex-query mocks in 4+ unrelated test fixtures purely for plumbing.
